items.b: GOLD IS $4,482.20 AND EVERY METAL ON THE TAPE IS WRITTEN BACK HIGHER
items.t: Against this paper's 19 August marks of record, gold is up $122.20 or 2.80%, silver $3.47 or 5.50%, platinum $73.00 or 4.23% and palladium $34.00 or 2.67%. Kitco at 06:02 New York, corroborated on TradingEconomics within 0.25% on gold and silver.

items.b: PLATINUM AND PALLADIUM COME OFF A HOLD FOR THE OPPOSITE REASON TO YESTERDAY'S
items.t: The 04:59 tape correctly held both, because the two pages were 0.85% and 1.57% apart. By press time the held marks of $1,726.00 and $1,274.00 sat below every live reading, so both are written at Kitco's $1,799.00 and $1,308.00.

items.b: THE TWO OUTSIDE SOURCES DISAGREE ON PLATINUM'S DIRECTION, NOT JUST ITS LEVEL
items.t: Kitco has platinum down 0.94% on the session, TradingEconomics up 0.18%. On level the two pages are $14.80 apart on platinum and $20.50 on palladium, a third consecutive session above 1.4%.

items.b: GOLD CLOSED ABOVE $4,500 ON 19 AUGUST AND IS BACK UNDER IT THIS MORNING
items.t: Kitco reported $4,518.90 on the day, up about 4%, session high $4,524.50, the first move above $4,500 since early June, after the Treasury said it would roughly double buybacks in 10-to-30-year maturities from 9 September.

items.b: THE 30-YEAR TREASURY YIELD FELL AS MUCH AS 10 BASIS POINTS TO 5.18%
items.t: The 10-year fell 6 basis points to 4.65%. This paper printed 5.31% for the long bond yesterday as a 19-year high. Both second-page sources name the bond market rather than metals demand as the driver.

items.b: SWISS WATCH EXPORTS ROSE 9.6% IN JULY AND THE YEAR TURNED POSITIVE
items.t: Total exports were CHF 2,628.3 million and the seven-month cumulative moved to plus 0.9%, from minus 0.7% at the half. Wristwatches were up 9.8% by value on 6.8% more units, 97,000 additional watches.

items.b: PRECIOUS METAL WAS 2.4% OF SWISS WRISTWATCH UNITS AND 36.2% OF THE VALUE
items.t: It was also the slowest-growing material by value at plus 3.7%, on plus 0.9% units. Gold-steel ran the other way, 4.4% fewer watches at an average export price up 29.5% by this desk's arithmetic.

items.b: INDIA SETS A $100 BILLION EXPORT TARGET FOR 2040 AND PUBLISHES NO INTERIM MILESTONE
items.t: From about $28 billion in 2025-26, the roadmap needs 9.5% compound growth a year in dollars to FY2039-40. Gross exports grew 2.44% in dollars across April to July, and 13.58% in rupees.

items.b: WHAT DID NOT PRINT TODAY, AND WHICH DESKS ARE DARK
items.t: The Doyle vintage American watch result could not be verified on this desk's own search and was cut, so auctions is dark a third edition. Gemstones is dark an eighth, correctly, on its Tuesday and Friday cadence, with its next file due 21 August. Retail-tech is dark a second on a genuinely dry beat.
